artworks.title: Exercises de l'hercule prussien
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a strongman struggling under the weight of multiple loads arranged on his back. The scene is depicted before an audience seated under a large tent. The strongman is on the ground, dressed as a performer with a helmet and is attempting to lift the substantial weight with evident strain. His facial expression and posture convey the challenge of the task. The people in the audience are sketched in a manner that captures their attention and possible amusement, suggesting that this is a moment of public spectacle. The tent and the audience create a backdrop that frames the main focus of the drawing, emphasizing the strongman's efforts. The drawing style is expressive, using character exaggeration to enhance the narrative and humor.

artworks.title: Le Président de la diète
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows the upper body of a man seated at a desk. The man is leaning back in his chair with his head tilted upward, looking above with a wide-eyed expression. He has a round face, a prominent nose, a thick neck, and sparse hair on the top of his head, with side whiskers on either side. His clothing consists of a dark jacket over a buttoned vest, with a necktie visible. His arms rest on the armrests of the chair. On the desk in front of him are papers, a quill pen in an inkwell, a hat, and a bell. Above the man, two swords hang by their tips over his head, labeled "Prusse" (Prussia) and "Autriche" (Austria). The background consists of swirling shaded lines. The text at the bottom of the image reads "Le Président de la diète, ou le double Damoclès!" referring to the man portrayed as the President of the Diet, with a double Sword of Damocles metaphor.

artworks.title: Un inventeur qui craint que son fonds ne luis reste ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a caricatured figure sitting on a pile of cannonballs with a cannon beside them, while a group of onlookers observe.

artworks.title: Cocher! La main de notre fille!
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of several figures in theatrical poses. Some figures are kneeling and raising their arms dramatically towards a seated figure. The setting is dramatized, with exaggerated expressions and poses. The lines and expressions are bold, conveying urgency and drama. The style includes detailed linework, resembling a caricature or satirical illustration.

artworks.title: Concert européen
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows a person sitting on a cannon surrounded by a large orchestra. The figure is clad in Roman-like armor. The orchestra, led by a conductor, consists of many musicians playing wind instruments. The scene is dynamic, with bold lines and exaggerated expressions. The style is similar to caricature art with satirical elements. The setting implies a blend of military and musical themes, humorously suggesting a 'concert of war.'

artworks.title: Renouvelée de la fontaine
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is an illustration of a knight with a horse's head surrounded by sheep. The knight is wearing heavy armor and holding a spear, standing among sheep with names like "HESSI," "BADEN," and "HANOVER." The sheep have fluffy textures and the background is a rolling landscape. The phrase "Renouvelé de Lafontaine" is included in the image. The style is satirical and whimsical, showcasing the absurdity of the scene.

artworks.title: Les augures modernes ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows two stylized individuals standing facing each other. The person on the left has a round face, glasses, short hair, and a peaked cap with a tassel. They are wearing a robe-like garment, knee-length skirt, and boots, holding a book titled “Notes”. The person on the right has a long face, angular features, a peaked cap with a feather, a robe, boots, and a book with a clasp. Both individuals stand on plain ground in the image. The background consists of faint lines at the edges of the page, emphasizing the figures.

artworks.title: Que faites-vous donc la avec ces civières
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows two people in a room. One person on the left is standing upright, facing another individual. They have distinct facial features and are wearing formal attire including a tall top hat and a long coat. The other person on the right is standing with a slightly hunched posture, gesturing with their right hand. They have sharp features and are wearing casual or work-related attire. The room contains furniture, and there are faint outlines of two more figures in the background. The setting is monochrome and sketch-like.

artworks.title: Pauvre vieux
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures. One figure, labeled "EQUILIBRE EUROPEEN," leans on crutches. The other figure, labeled "CONFERENCE," bends down towards the first figure. Underneath them, there is a line and the words "- Pauvre vieux!" depicting a scene that may symbolize a state of affairs in European politics. The drawing features exaggerated facial features and body postures, typical of satirical illustrations.

artworks.title: Pourvu que l'aiguilleur ne fasse rien dérailler!
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a railway junction with multiple signposts indicating different directions. The scene is depicted in a monochromatic style, showing a figure operating a lever to switch railway tracks. Around them are various signposts with inscriptions such as "Extrême Droite", "Droite Cauch", and "Centre Droit", among others. The artwork uses strong lines and cross-hatching to create a sense of depth and texture, emphasizing the tracks converging and diverging. The setting appears to be at a railway station or junction, with a train in the background on one of the tracks. The overcast sky is represented with cloud formations.

artworks.title: Les vendanges a Argenteuil
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows a side view of two full-length figures standing. The man stands with an upright posture while holding an umbrella above him with both hands. He has an elongated face with a prominent nose and is looking forward; his hair is covered by a cap. He is dressed in a dark vest over a long-sleeved shirt and light-colored trousers. Behind him, a woman holds a smaller umbrella, resting it on her shoulder while following him closely. Her long, wavy hair flows down her back, and her profile shows a calm expression. She wears a long dress that reaches the ground. In the background, there is a crowd of people, most of them bent forward. The background is filled with dense lines indicating a busy and crowded scene.

artworks.title: Mr. et Mme Prudhomme prenant un ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows two main characters in the foreground: a male figure wearing a Roman-style helmet and a female figure standing close by. The male figure has exaggerated facial features, a comical grin, and is dressed in a tunic with a cloak. The female figure wears a similar outfit and has curly hair. Several other figures in 19th-century Western clothing appear in the background. The scene is set against an architectural backdrop of columns and a high ceiling.

artworks.title: Chargé ... de garder les insignes de la souverainté
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts a person sitting on a large, striped trunk with their legs crossed and arms crossed over their chest. The person has a comical facial expression, and is wearing glasses, curly hair styled in a bob with a hat, and a long, flowing dress with detailed sleeves and buttons. To the left is an ornate chair, and the background has draped fabric and a piece of cloth on the floor.

artworks.title: Que diable est-ce qu'ils font la-haut!
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is an illustration of a figure submerged in water with a surprised expression. Another small figure is falling from above. The illustration shows a large, muscular figure with long hair seated on the ground and looking up. The setting includes a water current from a pipe on the left side. The background has textured shading suggesting movement. A smaller figure with exaggerated limbs falls to the right. The composition uses a monochromatic palette with contrasts in shading. It is captioned in French.

artworks.title: Pauvre vieux! T'es comme moi ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts an older soldier or sailor leaning against a cannon on a revolving platform. There is smoke in the background along with the dome of a building. The style is characterized by strong lines and expressive features, typical of satirical artwork. There is a signature and some text visible in the image.

artworks.title: Je t'en avais comblé ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a person trapped under a pile of sacks labeled '0000000'. Numerous sacks are piled on top of each other, each displaying the number '0000000'. Under the weight of this pile is a figure lying prone and seemingly struggling. The sacks symbolize a significant load, possibly conveying a theme of being overwhelmed. The image is framed with the word "ACTUALITÉS" at the top. French text below the image reads "Je t'en avais comblé, je t'en veux accabler," which roughly translates to "I had filled you, I now want to overwhelm you." The style is reminiscent of a traditional illustration emphasizing line work and shading for depth and texture.

artworks.title: Le hic c'est quand il s'agit de lui mettre une tête
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows a sculpture of a seated figure without a head, draped in a flowing robe and holding a scepter-like object in its right hand. The sculpture is depicted in a monochrome color scheme in a line drawing style, suggesting it is made of stone or a similar material. It is elevated on a pedestal labeled "MONARCHIE." In the foreground, a group of people holding small busts look up towards the sculpture in a caricature style, providing scale and context to its size.

artworks.title: Nos saltimbanques
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts a caricature featuring three full-bodied figures and one partial figure. There is a person on the left standing with arms crossed, a bald head with side hair, exaggerated eyebrows, a thick mustache and beard, wearing a short-sleeved shirt and pants. Next to this figure, another fully visible figure is lifting two smaller figures above their head. The lifter has bulging eyes, overemphasized features, and wears a striped garment, likely a vest and shorts. The two smaller figures being lifted have similar exaggerated facial features. The bottom figure, hoisted upside down, has short, curly hair and simple attire, while the topmost figure is also upside down, dressed similarly with visible facial expressions. In the background, there is a vague, indistinguishable shape and lightly drawn outlines, without specific context or setting details. The image also includes some French text at the bottom.

artworks.title: Assaut de la tribune
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a political caricature. The upper section is labeled "Assaut de la tribune" showing a chaotic scene with exaggerated figures in a parliamentary setting. The lower section, labeled "Salle d'attente – On demande Mⁿ Ferdinand," portrays a waiting room scene with exaggerated figures interacting. The drawing uses strong pencil lines and shading to emphasize the exaggerated features. It provides a satirical look at political and social situations, possibly drawing inspiration from contemporary events.

artworks.title: Un discours fatiguant pour le président
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two scenes in an assembly setting. The top scene shows a speaker at a podium, while the president of the assembly appears exhausted and tired. The audience in the background is depicted with simple rounded shapes. In the lower scene, two figures are shown in humorous poses. The characters are exaggerated in style, typical of caricature art.

artworks.title: Vois-tu, le petit estancelin comme il parle ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a black and white illustration of a satirical assembly scene. The drawing depicts a court or an assembly hall with people sitting on benches. One figure is gesturing forward and speaking while a smaller figure faces them. Two women with bonnet-shaped headgear and others are observing. In the lower section, exaggerated figures seem to be in a frantic or heated discussion. Two men in the foreground are holding each other's arms. French text above and below the images suggests a satirical commentary.

artworks.title: Mexican Orchestra
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Jack and Margrit Vanderryn)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a scene at a marketplace or fair under a large tent. The composition features figures engaged in musical performance and recreational activities. At the center, a group of musicians is seated in a semi-circle, with one playing a double bass and others playing violins. The figures wear wide-brimmed hats. More figures are engaged in games or conversations. On the left side, a table is decorated with various objects. The tent is illuminated by hanging lights, casting warm tones over the scene and creating shadows. The drawing captures a sense of community and shared enjoyment, portrayed through dynamic lines and a warm color palette of browns and ochres.

artworks.title: Au coq du brûyeres
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Jack and Margrit Vanderryn)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an outdoor cafe or garden scene. The image shows a crowded outdoor setting with tables occupied by patrons under large leafy trees. A waiter is walking through with a tray. A table with plates and drinks is on the left, and a raised swing is on the right. Additional figures are seated, engaging in conversations. The background shows a building structure. The scene captures a moment of social interaction and relaxation.

artworks.title: Marché à la terraille
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Jack and Margrit Vanderryn)
artworks.description: The image depicts a bustling market scene viewed from a slightly elevated angle. Tall buildings and trees obscure the horizon. The composition features intricate and detailed etched lines to create texture and depth. The color palette is monochromatic with shades of black, white, and gray. Various people are engaged in activities like inspecting items, conversing, and bartering. Additional figures and stands suggest ongoing market activities in the distance. Trees and buildings line the background.
